patterns.card_title: One surface. Agent and user, same state.
patterns.card_desc: The agent reads and writes the same canvas your users work on.
patterns.sub: Chat is an input, not the product. Shared state lets your agent read and write the same surface your users work on. Sidebar chatbots summarize. Agent-native apps act — same canvas, same state, human in the loop.
steps: Subscribe
useAgent hands you the agent and re-renders your components on every state change it emits.
Read
Render from agent.state like any other prop. Notes the agent writes show up in your panels, not in a chat bubble.
Write
Call agent.setState from your UI. On its next turn the agent reads it back — your users steer the model without typing.

patterns.meta_desc: Build agent-native apps where the agent reads and writes the same canvas your users work on. Live demo, code, and the guide.

patterns.card_desc: Agents render real components from tool calls — whatever the moment needs.
patterns.sub: Text walls are where agent UX goes to die. Render real components from tool calls instead. Controlled, declarative, or open-ended — three types of generative UI, one runtime, driven by your design system.
steps: Register
useComponent takes a name, a Zod schema for the props, and the component. The runtime exposes it to the agent as a tool.
Let the agent choose
When the user asks for a chart, the model picks render_bar_chart and streams the payload in.
Render
Zod validates the arguments, then your component renders inline — and can update as the payload fills.
patterns.meta_title: Generative UI: components, not paragraphs | CopilotKit
patterns.meta_desc: Render real components from agent tool calls instead of text walls. Three types of generative UI, one runtime. Live demo, code, and the guide.

patterns.card_desc: Specialized sub-agents behind one UI — handoffs, interrupts, shared state.
patterns.sub: Route one conversation across specialized sub-agents without losing state or context. Orchestrate them behind one UI — handoffs, interrupts, and shared state included — and show your users who is doing what.
steps: One supervisor
A supervisor agent owns the conversation and delegates to research, writing, or any sub-agent as tool calls.
One renderer per sub-agent
useRenderTool surfaces each delegation inline — the user sees which agent is running which task.
One state
Delegations, interrupts, and results live in shared state, so nothing is lost between handoffs.
patterns.meta_title: Multi-agent flows that stay coherent | CopilotKit
patterns.meta_desc: Route one conversation across specialized sub-agents without losing state or context. Live demo, code, and the guide.

patterns.card_desc: Ship the agent you already built to Slack, Teams, and beyond.
patterns.sub: Same agent, new channels. Don't rebuild the agent for every surface — Channels take the in-app agent you already built to Slack and beyond, where your users already work: threads, mentions, actions.
steps: Keep the agent
makeAgent returns the same agent that powers your app — one per thread, so conversations never mix.
Connect the channel
createChannel binds it to a Slack app through Intelligence. Credentials and provider routing stay out of your code.
Ship where users are
Mentions, threads, and interactive approvals work in-channel, with tool status visible as it runs.
patterns.meta_title: One agent, every channel: ship to Slack | CopilotKit
patterns.meta_desc: Take the in-app agent you already built to Slack, Teams, and beyond with Channels. Try it live, see the code, read the guide.

patterns.card_desc: The agent proposes, your user approves. Guardrails and an audit trail by default.
patterns.sub: LOB copilots earn trust with human-in-the-loop approval: the agent proposes, your user approves. Human-in-the-loop by default means the agent does the work inside your workflows, and your user stays in control.
steps: The agent proposes
Before a consequential action it calls request_user_approval with the concrete numbers and IDs.
Your UI decides
The handler returns a Promise. Your modal, outside the chat, resolves it with Approve or Reject.
The agent continues
The decision comes back as the tool result. Approved actions run; rejected ones stop, with the reason on record.
